# Results — Study 677 (Market Facilitation Index)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Bill
Williams' **BW-MFI** (`(High-Low)/Volume`), crossed against volume's own bar-to-bar
direction, names four bar "colors" — **Green** (MFI up, Volume up) should signal the move
is "in gear" and **continue**; **Squat** (MFI down, Volume up) should signal a coiled,
about-to-**reverse** market. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).*

No survivorship: every tape is a single continuously-traded ETF, not a cross-sectional
basket of names that can be dropped from the sample.

## The headline — forward return & continuation score by bar color (SPY)

`fwd_ret` = the return earned holding from the close of the colored bar to the next
close. `cont_score = sign(today's return) × fwd_ret` — **positive** means tomorrow
continued today's direction, **negative** means it reversed. The claim: Green should
show a *positive* continuation score above baseline; Squat should show a *negative* one.

| state | n | fwd ret (bps) | rest (bps) | Welch *t* (fwd) | cont score (bps) | rest (bps) | Welch *t* (cont) | continuation rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Green** | 1,954 | +6.64 | +4.19 | +0.84 | **−4.29** | −1.80 | **−0.85** | 46.5% |
| Fade | 2,002 | +3.68 | +5.10 | −0.48 | +2.35 | −3.86 | +2.08 | 49.6% |
| Fake | 2,256 | +6.76 | +4.02 | +0.94 | −6.07 | −1.02 | −1.74 | 49.1% |
| **Squat** | 2,196 | +2.01 | +5.73 | −1.26 | **−1.19** | −2.80 | **+0.54** | 48.6% |

Neither of the claim's two named states clears the desk's **|t| ≥ 2** bar, and both point
the *wrong* way: Green's continuation score is **negative** (−4.29 bps, *t* = −0.85) — the
opposite of "continuation" — and Squat's is barely below its own baseline (*t* = +0.54,
not the claimed reversal). Fade and Fake are incidental to the claim (not part of the
pre-registered continuation/reversal pair) but are reported in full for transparency;
Fake's cont-score *t* = −1.74 is the largest in magnitude on this single tape and still
doesn't clear 2.

**Label-shuffle placebo** (2,000 draws, reassigns the state label to a random same-size
subset of days, keeping every continuation score fixed): Green's observed gap of −2.48 bps
sits at **p = 0.4008**; Squat's +1.60 bps gap sits at **p = 0.5842**. Both are squarely
inside the shuffled-label null — indistinguishable from noise.

| **Squat** | 11,364 | +1.32 | −2.89 | −1.00 | **+1.35** | 48.3% |

Pooling six tickers (~50,000 state-days) doesn't rescue either named claim: Green's

still on the "wrong" side of their own claim. (Fake's pooled *t* = −2.07 nominally clears
2 — see the per-ticker check below for why that single crossing isn't certified either.)

## Per-ticker check — does the sign even hold up? (continuation score Welch *t*)

| ticker | Green *t* (n) | Squat *t* (n) |
|---|--:|--:|
| SPY | −0.85 (1,954) | +0.54 (2,196) |
| QQQ | −0.37 (1,699) | +1.31 (1,680) |
| DIA | −0.02 (1,432) | +0.92 (2,057) |
| IWM | +0.21 (1,396) | −0.13 (1,800) |
| XLE | +0.02 (1,234) | +0.58 (2,168) |
| GLD | +0.39 (1,149) | −0.23 (1,463) |

The sign **flips across tickers** for both states — Green is negative on SPY/QQQ/DIA and
positive on IWM/XLE/GLD; Squat is positive on four tapes and negative on two. Six
independent instruments, none individually significant, no consistent sign: this is what
noise looks like, not a six-way replication of a real effect. (Fake's nominal pooled
crossing above is driven by a handful of tapes and doesn't survive this same per-ticker
scrutiny — not shown in the pre-registered pair, mentioned only for completeness.)

## The timer — trading the colors, net of costs, vs buy-and-hold (SPY)

Two state-conditioned rules, one execution lag, one-way costs × NAV per flip:

- **Green filter** — long only while today's bar is Green ("in gear," ride the
  continuation), flat otherwise.
- **Squat avoidance** — always long *except* flat on a Squat bar (sidestep the claimed
  "about to reverse" day).
- **SMA(50/200)** — the obvious simpler trend benchmark, no volume term at all.

| rule | net Sharpe | buy-hold Sharpe | mean diff (bps/day) | HAC *t* (diff) | flips/yr |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Green filter** | 0.33 | 0.65 | **−3.630** | **−3.55** | 52.0 |
| Squat avoidance | 0.61 | 0.65 | −0.966 | −1.53 | 55.5 |
| SMA(50/200) | 0.75 | 0.65 | −0.719 | −0.97 | 0.5 |

The Green filter isn't merely flat versus buy-and-hold — it **loses to it significantly**
(HAC *t* = −3.55 net), and the gap survives at **zero cost** (*t* = −3.14, see the sweep
below): being long only on "in-gear" days misses too much of the market's underlying drift
to break even, let alone add value. Squat avoidance is statistically indistinguishable
from staying fully invested (*t* = −1.53). The volume-free SMA(50/200) crossover — which
needs none of BW-MFI's machinery — posts the best Sharpe of the three.

## Cost sweep — Green filter (SPY)

| one-way cost | net Sharpe | HAC *t* (vs buy-hold) |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bp | 0.45 | −3.14 |
| 1.0 bp | 0.33 | −3.55 |
| 2.0 bp | 0.21 | −3.95 |
| 5.0 bp | −0.15 | −5.17 |

Even **gross** (0 bp), the Green filter is significantly worse than simply holding SPY.
This isn't a cost story — the underperformance is structural (missing 77% of the tape's
trading days without a compensating edge on the days it keeps).

**Sign-permutation placebo** on the Green-filter timer (1,000 draws, real position vector
randomly reordered): the real strategy-minus-benchmark Sharpe gap is **−0.314**, and
**21.1%** of random reorderings of the same exposure profile do at least as poorly — the
timer's underperformance is not even an unusually bad draw of its own exposure schedule.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic tape whose day-to-day range and volume are two independent AR(1)-in-logs
processes (unrelated to the return path — exactly like the real mechanics, where a bar's
range and volume are set by that session's trading, not by tomorrow's return), classified
into the same four BW states; a TUNABLE knob plants a Green-continuation /
Squat-reversal effect. No network.

| world | Green cont score | Green Welch *t* | Squat cont score | Squat Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| null (planted = 0), **20 seeds** | mean *t* **+0.35** (sd 0.87) | \|t\|≥2 in 1/20 | mean *t* **−0.17** (sd 0.76) | \|t\|≥2 in 0/20 |
| planted = +0.6 (seed 677) | **+70.42 bps** | **+17.23** | **−63.65 bps** | **−22.14** |

The detector all but never fires on the null (1/20 seeds — in line with a nominal ~5%
false-positive rate under repeated testing, not a systematic bias) and lights up sharply
on a planted effect in both directions at once. The machinery is unbiased; the near-zero
real-tape *t*'s above (−0.85 / +0.54 on SPY, −0.33 / +1.35 pooled) are the genuine
absence of an effect, not a blind detector. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never
cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Neither of the claim's two named states clears **t ≥ 2** on the real
  tape: Green's continuation score is **−0.85** on SPY (**−0.33** pooled across 6
  tickers, ~50k state-days), Squat's is **+0.54** on SPY (**+1.35** pooled) — both under
  the bar, both nominally on the *wrong* side of the claim, and the sign flips
  ticker-by-ticker with no consistent pattern. The label-shuffle placebo confirms both
  (*p* = 0.40 / 0.58): statistically indistinguishable from a random subset of days the
  same size.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The one tradeable expression of the claim — go long only on
  Green days — **loses significantly to buy-and-hold** (HAC *t* = −3.55 net, −3.14 even
  gross) and a volume-free SMA(50/200) crossover beats it outright with none of the
  machinery. Squat avoidance is a wash. There is no residual edge to charge costs against
  because there was never a signal to begin with.
- **"Green flags continuation, Squat flags reversal?" — BUSTED.** Both named
  predictions fail on the real tape, both fail the placebo, both flip sign across six
  independent instruments, and the one trading rule built on the "continuation" half
  actively underperforms simply holding the index. The synthetic control shows the
  harness *can* find this exact effect when it's really there (*t* > 17 at a modest
  planted knob) — it simply isn't there in the market.
